text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Islamist-led government gearing up to impose a ban on satellite dishes in southeast Turkey to prevent people from watching the pro-Kurdish Med TV.
- President Suleyman Demirel says he has not got used to the newly-issued five million lira banknotes.
- Jury of leading doctors and health officials chooses Turkey's top ten hospitals.
- Some four million Turks possess handguns or hunting rifles.
- Justice minister dismisses symbolic "lights-out" protests against security scandal.
- Russian ambassador to Ankara says his country is ready to help in keeping the Bosphorus and Dardanelles straits clean.
- Jewellers take advantage of new opportunities for gold banking, but Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's plans to raise funds from jewellers declaring their stocks fail.
- Turkish intelligence service hides information from authorities investigating a security scandal.
